hints: Remember that a zero overall dipole does not mean no polar bonds, it means the bond dipoles cancel by symmetry.
Notice that Cl is much more electronegative than C and H, so every C-Cl bond is polar with the negative end on Cl.
Compare the tetrahedral shapes and ask yourself in which molecule all four bond dipoles pull equally in opposite directions to cancel out completely.
walkthrough:
**What zero dipole moment means**

Think of dipole moment as the tug of war between bond dipoles. It is zero only when polar bonds are arranged so symmetrically that all the pulls cancel.

Rule to use:
$$\text{overall dipole} = \text{vector sum of bond dipoles} = 0 \text{ for perfect symmetry}$$

**Check the bond polarity**

Chlorine is more electronegative than carbon and hydrogen. So each $\text{C-Cl}$ bond has a strong dipole toward Cl, while $\text{C-H}$ is almost non-polar.

This means $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{CHCl}_3$ all have unbalanced pulls because $\text{C-Cl}$ and $\text{C-H}$ are different.

**Check the symmetry**

All four molecules are basically tetrahedral around carbon. Only $\text{CCl}_4$ has four identical $\text{C-Cl}$ bonds pointing to the four corners of a perfect tetrahedron.

The four equal dipoles cancel exactly, so the overall dipole moment is zero.

options.A: Incorrect. In $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ there is one strongly polar $\text{C-Cl}$ bond and three almost non-polar $\text{C-H}$ bonds. There is nothing to balance the $\text{C-Cl}$ pull, so the molecule has a net dipole.
options.B: Incorrect. In $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ the two $\text{C-Cl}$ dipoles are on the same side of the tetrahedron and do not point in opposite directions. They add together to give a net dipole, a common trap if you think two identical bonds always cancel.
options.C: Incorrect. In $\text{CHCl}_3$ the three $\text{C-Cl}$ dipoles partly cancel each other, but the single $\text{C-H}$ bond is very different. The arrangement is unsymmetrical, so a net dipole remains.
options.D: Correct. $\text{CCl}_4$ is perfectly tetrahedral with four identical polar $\text{C-Cl}$ bonds. The symmetry means the four bond dipole vectors sum to zero, so the molecule is non-polar overall despite having polar bonds. Well done for spotting the symmetry.
